events.title: Cicero is killed on Mark Antony's orders
events.description: Proscribed by the Second Triumvirate, Marcus Tullius Cicero was overtaken by soldiers near Formiae and killed. His head and hands were displayed in the Forum, where he had attacked Antony in his Philippics.
events.html: Proscribed by the Second Triumvirate, Marcus Tullius Cicero was overtaken by soldiers near Formiae and killed. His head and hands were displayed in the Forum, where he had attacked Antony in his Philippics.

events.title: Justin II proclaims his general Tiberius caesar
events.description: During a respite from a severe mental illness, the Eastern Roman emperor Justin II proclaimed his general Tiberius caesar and adopted him as his son. Tiberius became co-emperor in 578 and reigned until 582 as Tiberius II Constantine.

events.title: Apprentice boys shut the gates of Derry against a Jacobite force
events.description: In Derry, 13 apprentices shut the town's gates against Jacobite forces, an act of rebellion against James II. Its Protestant defenders went on to withstand a siege by James II's army for 105 days in 1689.

events.title: The mayor of Toruń and nine Lutheran officials are executed
events.description: After a Protestant crowd vandalised the Jesuit college in Toruń (Thorn) in Royal Prussia, the Polish supreme court blamed Mayor Johann Gottfried Rösner and nine other Lutheran officials for neglect of duty. They were sentenced to death and executed.

events.title: The Theatre Royal, Covent Garden, opens
events.description: John Rich opened his new theatre at Covent Garden with Congreve's The Way of the World. Twice rebuilt after fires, it became the Royal Opera House in 1892.
events.html: John Rich opened his new theatre at Covent Garden with Congreve's The Way of the World. Twice rebuilt after fires, it became the Royal Opera House in 1892.

events.title: Marshal Ney is executed by firing squad
events.description: Michel Ney, whom Napoleon called 'the bravest of the brave', was shot in Paris for treason after joining his former emperor during the Hundred Days. He refused a blindfold and is said to have given the order to fire.

events.title: Japan attacks Pearl Harbor
events.description: Japanese carrier aircraft struck the US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, killing more than 2,400 Americans and sinking or damaging 19 ships. The United States entered the Second World War the next day.
events.html: Japanese carrier aircraft struck the US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, killing more than 2,400 Americans and sinking or damaging 19 ships. The United States entered the Second World War the next day.

events.title: Indonesia invades East Timor
events.description: Indonesian forces invaded East Timor nine days after Fretilin declared independence from Portugal. The occupation cost an estimated 100,000 to 180,000 lives before a UN-supervised vote led to independence.
